topics.name: AI agents
topics.blurb: Agents, tools and MCP servers that actually work: scoping, tool design, multi-agent, memory, evals, Claude and other stacks.

superskill.description: Design, build, test and ship AI agents and their tools. Covers agent vs workflow and stack choice; tool design (names, schemas, errors, tool count); MCP servers (remote HTTP, stdio, MCPB, OAuth, elicitation, Inspector) and MCP apps with in-chat widgets; multi-agent orchestration and parallel sub-agents; context engineering, prompt caching, memory; agent system prompts; agent and MCP evals (rubrics, held-back sets, MCP eval harness); Claude API tool loops, Tool Runner, Agent SDK, Managed Agents; Vercel AI SDK, Mastra, LangGraph, Deep Agents, Google ADK, Cloudflare Agents, Microsoft Foundry; ElevenLabs voice agents. Use when asked to build an agent or chatbot with tools, wrap an API for Claude, build an MCP server or connector, add MCP widgets, split work across sub-agents, add memory to an agent, write an agent system prompt, evaluate or debug an agent, launch a managed or scheduled agent, or build a voice agent.

topics.name: Website building
topics.blurb: Brief to live URL: copy, a design that doesn't look AI-made, Next.js or Astro builds, Core Web Vitals, SEO, browser checks, deploys.

superskill.description: Plan, design, build, verify and ship websites that do not look AI-generated. Use for landing pages, marketing and product sites, portfolios, docs and blogs; writing page copy and CTAs or reviewing conversion (CRO); choosing a design direction, palette and type and avoiding generic "AI slop"; fixing pages that look boring or plain; picking Lenis, GSAP or component libraries; scroll storytelling, scroll-scrubbed video, parallax heroes and page motion; cinematic demo sites with an AI film hero (stills, image-to-video, frame sequence); Next.js App Router and React performance rules, Server Actions, Cache Components adoption and next dev runtime checks; Astro, Vue 3 and single-file HTML sites; Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS) audits and fixes; technical SEO, sitemaps, canonicals, hreflang, JSON-LD and AI crawler controls; Lighthouse, accessibility, Playwright browser tests and whole-site audits; deploying to Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Workers or Pages, env vars and failed builds.

Use when debugging any bug, failing or flaky test, build break or regression; doing TDD, writing or judging tests and mocks; verifying work before saying done, committing or opening a PR; reviewing code, a diff or a PR, or requesting a review; acting on review feedback or bot comments; simplifying, refactoring or cleaning up code, or keeping a change minimal and surgical; designing modules, interfaces, seams, domain glossaries or ADRs, or finding architecture hot spots; git commits, branches, worktrees, pre-commit hooks, blocking dangerous git commands, or finishing a branch (merge, PR, keep); and React or Next.js performance (waterfalls, bundle size, re-renders). topics.name: AI video
topics.blurb: Make, generate, edit and deliver video: HyperFrames, video-model prompts, ffmpeg cuts, captions, beat cuts and QA.

superskill.description: Make, edit, generate and deliver video with AI help. Covers picking the route (HyperFrames/HTML composition, text/image-to-video, footage edit, AI presenter); HyperFrames (composition contract, CLI check/render, registry, Studio, design spec, narration, beat plans, audio-reactive visuals); video-model prompts and APIs (Seedance, Wan, Kling, Gemini Omni/Veo, Runway, ByteDance ModelArk, fal, LTX-2, FLUX 3, HeyGen avatars); transcript cuts with ffmpeg (trim, fillers, 9:16 reframe, grade, EDL); captions, talking-head recuts; beat-cut music videos and films from AI stills; launch, promo, site-tour and explainer videos; real macOS screen recordings of web apps; delivery (loudness, safe zones, specs, QA). Use when asked to make a video, promo, product tour, explainer, reel/short, captioned clip, music video or beat cut, AI b-roll, animate a photo, screen-record a web app, edit/cut footage, add subtitles, write a video-model prompt, call a video API (Seedance, Runway, Veo), or export for TikTok/Reels/YouTube.

topics.name: Cloud & DevOps
topics.blurb: Ship and run apps: hosting choice, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Azure and observability.

superskill.description: Deploy, run and operate apps in the cloud. Covers choosing a host, Dockerfiles and Compose, Kubernetes manifests and debugging (GKE/EKS), Terraform/OpenTofu (style, state, modules, tests, safe destroy), GitHub Actions CI/CD (quality gates, OIDC, previews, rollbacks), Cloudflare Workers/Wrangler/Durable Objects, Google Cloud Run (incl. Next.js behind Firebase Hosting) and Firebase App Hosting, AWS (IAM, Lambda, ECS/EKS/ECR, CDK), Azure (azd, Container Apps/App Service diagnostics, KQL), and observability (OpenTelemetry, Grafana, RED/USE, alerts). Use when asked to deploy or ship an app, "put this live", write a Dockerfile or compose.yaml, shrink or harden an image, write k8s YAML or debug CrashLoopBackOff/Pending pods, write or review Terraform, set up a GitHub Actions pipeline, configure wrangler.jsonc, deploy to Cloud Run, fix gcloud "No module named grpc", write an IAM policy, build a Lambda, run azd up, add OpenTelemetry, build a Grafana dashboard, or debug a production outage.

topics.name: Testing & QA
topics.blurb: TDD, unit and E2E tests (Playwright, Cypress, pytest, Vitest, Go), browser QA, flaky-test fixes, property and mutation testing.

superskill.description: Plan, write, run and fix automated tests, and QA running apps. Use for test strategy (unit vs integration vs API vs component vs E2E, what to mock, coverage); TDD red-green-refactor and writing tests that catch real bugs; Playwright E2E tests (locators, web-first assertions, auth storageState, network mocking, config, traces, CI sharding); driving a browser to verify or debug a web app (Python Playwright with a server helper, playwright-cli, Chrome DevTools); exploratory QA with health scores, issue reports and a fix loop; flaky tests (classify, root cause, prove in CI); pytest, Vitest/Jest, Go, JUnit 5, Swift Testing; Cypress E2E and component tests; mobile UI flows on simulators, Flutter widget tests; property-based and mutation testing. Triggers: "write tests", "add a regression test", "TDD", "E2E test", "test this flow", "QA my app", "this test is flaky", "increase coverage", "why did CI fail".

topics.name: Figma & design systems
topics.blurb: Figma MCP, tokens and variables, code-Figma sync and drift, component and screen-reader specs, hand-off, design-to-code and audits.

superskill.description: Work with Figma files and design systems through the Figma MCP server or other design bridges. Use for reading Figma frames without wasting calls; safe canvas writes with use_figma; design tokens and Figma variables (tiers, naming, modes, scopes, code syntax, DTCG, Style Dictionary, Tailwind v4); syncing tokens between Figma and code, drift and parity checks; component specs and docs (API, anatomy, structure, colour, uSpec); accessibility and screen-reader specs (VoiceOver, TalkBack, ARIA); hand-off specs; implementing Figma designs as code that reuses existing components and tokens; design-system audits and fixes; building variables, components and libraries in Figma; Penpot and OpenPencil (.fig). Says when to load Figma's own skills (figma-use, figma-design-to-code, figma-generate-library, figma-code-connect). Triggers: "implement this Figma frame", "export our Figma variables", "sync tokens", "spec this component", "screen reader spec", "audit our design system", "hand-off doc".

topics.name: Token efficiency
topics.blurb: Fewer tokens, same quality: session hygiene, lean context, caching that hits, model and effort choice, batch, plan limits and cost.

superskill.description: Spend fewer tokens and less money with Claude and other LLMs without losing quality, in Claude Code or agent sessions and in apps that call an LLM API. Covers session hygiene (/clear vs /compact, reading file ranges, subagents that return short results); model and effort choice per task, cascades and routing; per-turn overhead from MCP tools, skills and CLAUDE.md, and compressing memory files; terse output (caveman mode) and when not to use it; prompt caching that actually hits; batch, semantic caching and max_tokens; retrieval vs long context; measuring usage and cost (usage fields, ccusage, cost per task) and staying within 5-hour or weekly plan limits. Triggers: "caveman mode", "use fewer tokens", "why did I hit my Claude limit", "where did my tokens go", "my context fills up too fast", "cut our LLM API bill", "cache_read_input_tokens is 0", "cheapest model for this", "compress my CLAUDE.md". Building the agent itself: ai-agents. CLAUDE.md, hooks and skills: claude-meta.

skills.name: caveman
skills.purpose: Terse 'caveman' answer style: answer first, no ceremony or hedging, short words, one idea per sentence, while code, commands, paths, numbers and negations stay verbatim. Cuts output tokens without dropping technical facts.
skills.how_to_use: Install with `npx skills add JuliusBrussee/caveman` or the Claude Code plugin (`claude plugin marketplace add JuliusBrussee/caveman`). Trigger with /caveman, 'be brief' or 'less tokens'; stays on until 'stop caveman'. /caveman ultra switches to the harder ultracave mode.
skills.evidence: Also ranked in claude_meta. skills.sh 556K installs, trending #88 (ultracave/megacave hot #5/#6 this week); README cites #1 GitHub Trending (Jul 2026); listed in hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code. Outside tests cited in README: JetBrains paired A/B (86 tasks, skill only) 8.5% fewer output tokens with no quality change; Adobe Research CAVEWOMAN paper 1.4-2.4x lower output cost.
skills.notes: Gains are modest in agentic coding (most tokens are input/tool output, which the skill does not touch). The skill folder itself is prompt-only. The repo's separate caveman CLI/proxy (driven by caveman-setup/-discover/-learn/-optimize) sends usage telemetry by default (opt out: `caveman telemetry off` or DO_NOT_TRACK=1), 'managed mode' tags requests with repo and branch for Caveman Cloud, and the README offers a curl | bash installer. Take the skill, not the engine.

skills.name: caveman-compress
skills.purpose: Rewrites memory files (CLAUDE.md, todo lists, preference notes) into compressed caveman prose to cut the input tokens they cost on every turn, keeping code, URLs, paths, commands and headings exact and saving a readable backup outside the tree.
skills.how_to_use: /caveman-compress <file>. Runs the bundled Python CLI (`python3 -m scripts <path>`), which calls Claude through the Anthropic SDK when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, otherwise `claude --print`; validates the output and retries up to twice.
skills.evidence: skills.sh 385.6K installs, trending #109 this week; same 109k-star repo as caveman.
skills.notes: Sends the file to Anthropic (official API or Claude CLI) only. Review the compressed file: terse rules can lose nuance; the README's own figures are byte sizes, not measured billing savings.

skills.name: cavecrew
skills.purpose: Decides when to delegate to three compressed-output subagents (investigator: locate code, builder: 1-2 file edits, reviewer: diff review) instead of working inline or using Explore, so each delegation returns about a third of the tokens to the main context.
skills.how_to_use: Ships with the caveman plugin, which also installs the cavecrew-investigator/-builder/-reviewer agent files. Triggers when choosing a subagent for search, small edits or review; use vanilla Explore when you want prose and rationale.
skills.evidence: skills.sh 333.6K installs, trending #116 this week; same repo as caveman.
skills.notes: Needs the agents/ files from the plugin; the skill alone does nothing. Same CLI telemetry caveat as caveman applies only if you install the caveman CLI.

skills.name: context-budget
skills.purpose: Audits what a Claude Code session loads every turn (agents, skills, rules, MCP servers and their tool schemas, CLAUDE.md) with token estimates, flags bloat such as >20-tool MCP servers, long descriptions and duplicate copies, and gives a ranked list of token savings.
skills.how_to_use: Run /context-budget or ask why context feels tight after adding skills/MCP servers. Read-only; estimates tokens as words x 1.3 and about 500 tokens per MCP tool.
skills.evidence: everything-claude-code (ECC), 272k stars; skills.sh 9.1K installs; ECC listed in hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code.

skills.name: strategic-compact
skills.purpose: Suggests manual /compact at logical phase boundaries (after research, before implementation, after a milestone) instead of letting auto-compaction cut mid-task; covers what survives compaction and trigger-table lazy loading to keep context lean.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers in long sessions near context limits; optional PreToolUse hook counts tool calls and nudges at a threshold. Pair with /clear between unrelated tasks.
skills.evidence: Also ranked in claude_meta. ECC 272k stars; skills.sh 10.6K installs; also on aitmpl.com as cc-skill-strategic-compact.
skills.notes: The hook is optional and local.

skills.name: cost-aware-llm-pipeline
skills.purpose: Patterns for cutting LLM API spend in apps: route by task complexity (cheap model first, strong model for hard items), immutable per-call cost tracking with a budget guard, retry only on transient errors, and prompt caching for long system prompts.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers when building or reviewing code that calls Claude/OpenAI APIs, batch-processing items, or when spend has to come down. Python examples; adapt model IDs and prices to current ones.
skills.evidence: ECC 272k stars; skills.sh 9.5K installs; copied into several forks (everything-claude-code-zh, skills-for-open-code).
skills.notes: Hard-coded model names and thresholds are examples; check current pricing.

skills.name: context-mode
skills.purpose: Keeps large tool output out of the context window: commands, logs, test output, API responses, browser snapshots and fetched docs run in a sandbox (ctx_execute / ctx_execute_file) or get indexed and searched (ctx_fetch_and_index / ctx_search), so only the relevant lines come back.
skills.how_to_use: Install the context-mode MCP server/plugin for Claude Code (also Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini). The skill tells the agent to use ctx_* tools for anything beyond a small Bash whitelist; /context-mode:ctx-stats shows savings.
skills.evidence: 25k stars since Feb 2026; skills.sh 2.7K installs (ctx-stats 1.6K, ctx-doctor 1.4K); named in the caveman and token-optimizer comparison tables.
skills.notes: Elastic License 2.0 (source-available, not OSI): link-only. README says no telemetry and everything stays local; the sibling ctx-insight skill only opens a hosted team dashboard.

skills.name: context-optimization

skills.how_to_use: Triggers when token cost or context limits hurt quality in an agent design; pairs with the same repo's context-compression, context-degradation and context-fundamentals skills.

skills.name: llm-cost-optimizer
skills.purpose: Cost engineering for LLM features in three modes (audit, optimize, design): model routing, prompt caching, output-length control, prompt compression, semantic caching and batching, each with expected savings, plus proactive flags like an unset max_tokens or a single model for every request.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on 'AI costs too high', 'which model should I use', 'implement prompt caching' or when an AI endpoint is being designed. Asks for traffic, models and spend first, then produces a ranked plan.
skills.evidence: 27k-star collection; skills.sh 80 installs (plus a borghei fork with 87).
skills.notes: Savings percentages are rules of thumb.

skills.name: prompt-caching
skills.purpose: LLM caching patterns: Anthropic cache_control on stable prefixes with cache-read/write monitoring, exact and semantic response caching (Redis), temperature-aware keys, cache-augmented generation (CAG) instead of RAG for small corpora, and invalidation pitfalls.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on prompt caching, response caching or CAG. TypeScript examples with @anthropic-ai/sdk and ioredis/Upstash.
skills.evidence: skills.sh 914 installs (plus 446 for the davila7/claude-code-templates copy, also on aitmpl.com); 47k-star collection.
skills.notes: Converted from vibeship-spawner-skills (Apache-2.0); example model IDs are dated. For diagnosing misses, see audit-prompt-caching.

skills.name: stay-within-limits
skills.purpose: Keeps long-running or parallel agent work inside the 5-hour and weekly plan limits: run bounded waves (default 3 subagents), check usage between waves, pause at 95% and schedule a self-contained resume, re-checking the real window on wake.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers for long or fan-out runs. In Claude Code it reads usage with `npx -y ccusage@latest blocks --active --json`; uses a wakeup/resume tool when the host has one.
skills.evidence: Builder.io's skills repo, created Jun 2026 and at 4.5k stars; skills.sh 304 installs.
skills.notes: npx fetches ccusage from npm on each run; pin a version if that matters. ccusage reads local logs only.

skills.name: efficient-fable
skills.purpose: Uses the top model (Claude Fable) only as orchestrator and judge, and pushes token-heavy research, inventory, test runs and bounded edits to cheaper subagents with tight handoff packets that ask for concise evidence (files, lines, diffs, stop conditions).
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on codebase-heavy or token-heavy work with Fable; the pattern applies to any expensive lead model. Needs subagents with a model override.
skills.evidence: skills.sh 833 installs; Builder.io repo created Jun 2026, 4.5k stars.

skills.name: token-optimizer

skills.how_to_use: Install the token-optimizer plugin; run /token-optimizer when context feels tight. Siblings: token-coach, token-dashboard, fleet-auditor, resume-checkpoint.
skills.evidence: 2.5k stars; skills.sh 876 installs (token-coach 353, fleet-auditor 333).
skills.notes: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (plus a small-business permission): link-only. README states zero telemetry and no network calls. The skill tells the agent never to suggest removing its own skills.

skills.name: rtk-optimizer
skills.purpose: Wraps verbose shell commands (git log/status/diff, find, cat, test runners, cargo, pnpm) with RTK so their output is compressed 50-90% before it enters the context window, and tracks savings over the session.
skills.how_to_use: Needs the RTK CLI (`brew install rtk-ai/tap/rtk` or `cargo install rtk`). Triggers on high-verbosity commands; suggests the rtk-prefixed form and runs it once confirmed.
skills.evidence: Example skill in the 6.1k-star Claude Code Ultimate Guide; skills.sh 255 installs; RTK itself (rtk-ai/rtk) has 82k stars.
skills.notes: RTK's telemetry is opt-in and off by default (RTK_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 blocks it); its README's curl | sh installer is avoidable via brew/cargo. CC-BY-SA requires attribution and share-alike.

skills.name: redis-semantic-cache
skills.purpose: Semantic caching of LLM responses with Redis LangCache: cache-aside flow (search, then call the model on a miss and store), similarity-threshold tuning for hit rate vs precision, separate caches per task type, and attribute filters.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers when caching completions or RAG answers to cut API cost and latency. Needs a Redis Cloud LangCache instance (HOST, CACHE_ID, API_KEY) and the langcache SDK or REST API.
skills.evidence: Official Redis; skills.sh 1.7K installs; redis/agent-skills listed in VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills.
skills.notes: LangCache is a preview Redis Cloud service: prompts and responses are stored there (vendor's own service). Self-hosted alternative: Redis vector search.

skills.name: exploring-llm-costs

skills.name: chisle

topics.name: Presentations
topics.blurb: Deck story, slide design, PowerPoint, HTML, Slidev, Marp, Google Slides and Keynote decks, speaker notes, rehearsal and delivery.

superskill.description: Make and give presentations in any format. Covers deck story and structure (pitch deck, investor and sales decks, board and status updates, decision decks, conference and tech talks, lectures, research talks, defenses), slide design and layout (grid, type, colour, density, one idea per slide), data slides, PowerPoint/.pptx with PptxGenJS or python-pptx, filling or editing a template deck, HTML and Markdown decks (single-file, Slidev, Marp, reveal.js, Beamer), Google Slides and Keynote, image-generated slides, PDF export, speaker notes, rehearsal, timing, delivery and Q&A, and render-and-look deck QA. Triggers: "make a deck on this", "pitch deck for our seed round", "turn this doc into slides", "fill our PowerPoint template", "build a Slidev talk", "write my speaker notes", "my talk runs over time", "help me rehearse my presentation", "export the slides to PDF". Word, PDF and Excel files: docs-office.

skills.name: pptx

skills.how_to_use: Triggers whenever a .pptx/.potx file is involved or a PowerPoint deck is requested. Bundled in claude.ai and Claude Code document skills; needs Python (python-pptx, markitdown), Node (pptxgenjs) and LibreOffice (soffice) for rendering checks.

skills.name: ppt-master
skills.purpose: Routed workflow that turns documents, notes or briefs into natively editable PPTX: strategist/executor roles, design spec and spec lock, reusable Brand/Style/Layout workspaces, filling native templates, rebuilding page visuals, beautifying finished decks, and narrated or self-running video output.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on create/redesign/template/fill/enhance a PPT or deck, or 'ppt-master'. Clone the repo or install the skill folder; needs Python 3 with its requirements. AI images are optional and use your own provider key (OpenAI-compatible, MiniMax, etc.).

topics.name: Open models
topics.blurb: Open-weight LLMs: model and licence choice, VRAM maths, Ollama and llama.cpp, vLLM, RunPod and Modal, GGUF, LoRA fine-tunes and evals.

superskill.description: Run, serve, fine-tune and evaluate open-weight models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, DeepSeek, gpt-oss), instead of or beside paid APIs. Covers picking a model and checking its weight licence for commercial use; VRAM, context and cost maths; running locally with Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio or MLX; serving with vLLM, SGLang and OpenAI-compatible endpoints; GPU hosting on RunPod, Modal and HF Jobs; GGUF, AWQ and GPTQ quantization; the Hugging Face Hub, hf CLI, transformers, datasets and Spaces; fine-tuning with LoRA/QLoRA, TRL, Unsloth or LlamaFactory; benchmarking with lm-eval-harness or lighteval; pointing agents and tools at a local model. Triggers: "run a model locally", "which open model fits my GPU", "can I use Llama commercially", "serve Qwen with vLLM", "deploy a model on RunPod", "quantize to GGUF", "fine-tune with LoRA", "hf download", "evaluate my fine-tune", "use Ollama with my agent". Image, video or audio generation recipes: image-creation, ai-video, audio-generation.

superskill.description: Design and teach courses, lessons and workshops for online, school (K-12, university) and corporate learning, and tutor one learner. topics.name: Email marketing
topics.blurb: Lists and consent, lifecycle flows, campaigns and A/B tests, deliverability, React Email and MJML, sending APIs, ESPs and email law.

superskill.description: Run email as a marketing and product channel end to end. Covers strategy, list growth, signup forms, lead magnets and double opt-in; segments; lifecycle flows (welcome, onboarding, nurture, abandoned cart, browse, post-purchase, win-back, sunset, dunning); campaigns, subject lines, preview text and A/B tests; deliverability (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI, warm-up, bounces, complaints, one-click unsubscribe, Gmail and Yahoo sender rules); transactional email; React Email and MJML templates, HTML email quirks, dark mode; sending APIs (Resend, Postmark, Amazon SES, SendGrid, Cloudflare Email); ESPs (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Customer.io, Loops, Kit); email metrics; CAN-SPAM, GDPR, PECR, CASL; small compliant cold emails. Triggers: "set up a welcome sequence", "abandoned cart flow", "our emails go to spam", "set up DMARC", "build this email in React Email", "send with Resend", "audit our Klaviyo", "grow my email list", "is this cold email legal". Writing one newsletter issue: content-creation.

topics.name: E-commerce
topics.blurb: Shopify and WooCommerce builds, store checkout and tax, catalogs and feeds, pricing, inventory, sales analytics and agent checkout.

superskill.description: Build and run an online store: platform, storefront, payments, products, stock and sales. Covers picking Shopify, WooCommerce, Medusa, Saleor or headless; Shopify themes (Liquid, theme check), apps and APIs (Admin and Storefront GraphQL, bulk operations, Functions, checkout extensions, Hydrogen), when to install Shopify's AI Toolkit; WooCommerce Store API, headless carts; store checkout (Stripe Checkout, subscriptions, Stripe Tax, marketplaces); catalogs, variants, CSV imports, bulk edits, catalog audits, Merchant Center feeds and API; product pages, store CRO; pricing, discounts, repricing; inventory, reorders, orders, fulfilment; store analytics (revenue drops, AOV, LTV, cohorts); agentic commerce (UCP, ACP). Triggers: "set up a Shopify store", "build a Liquid section", "bulk update prices", "why did sales drop", "what should I reorder", "fix Merchant Center disapprovals", "let AI agents buy from our store". Shopping ads: google-ads. Stripe outside a store: backend-databases.

skills.name: shopify
skills.purpose: Shopify's single official skill covering every developer surface: Admin and Storefront GraphQL, Customer Account API, Functions, Liquid themes, Hydrogen, Polaris admin/checkout/customer-account extensions, POS UI, metafields/metaobjects, ShopifyQL analytics, app pricing, App Store review and merchant onboarding (mock.shop preview stores). It routes each request to a topic guide, searches shopify.dev, and validates generated GraphQL/Liquid/Functions code before returning it.
skills.how_to_use: Install the Shopify AI Toolkit plugin (`claude plugin install shopify-ai-toolkit@claude-plugins-official` or `npx skills add shopify/shopify-ai-toolkit --skill shopify`). Triggers on any Shopify API, theme, extension, Function or 'make me a store' request; needs Node.js, and Shopify CLI for store execution.
skills.evidence: Official Shopify (toolkit docs at shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/ai-toolkit); in the official Claude plugin marketplace. skills.sh: the toolkit's skills total ~200K+ installs (shopify-admin 17.0K, shopify-liquid 13.0K, shopify-storefront-graphql 12.9K, shopify-dev 12.7K, shopify-functions 10.8K, shopify-hydrogen 9.7K ...); this unified `shopify` skill replaced them (1.4K installs under the new name). Ranked #3/#5/#6 on claudeskills.info's ecommerce list; shopify-storefront-graphql on skills.sh /hot.
skills.notes: link-only (security): telemetry. A PostToolUse hook and the bundled scripts report to shopify.dev/mcp/usage (Shopify's own host): search queries, validated code, model/client ids, session/tool-use ids and, when supplied, the verbatim user prompt (up to 2,000 chars). Opt out with OPT_OUT_INSTRUMENTATION=true or an empty ~/.config/shopify-ai-toolkit/opt-out file. The 20 older per-surface skills (shopify-admin, shopify-liquid, ...) now sit in deprecated/ as stubs pointing here. Content itself is MIT.

topics.name: Career & job search
topics.blurb: Resumes tailored to a posting, ATS checks, cover letters, job search, interview prep, salary negotiation, promotions and hiring.

superskill.description: Get a job and grow in one, with every claim kept true. Use for writing, reviewing or tailoring a resume or CV to a job description; ATS-safe formatting; cover letters and application answers; job search strategy, scoring postings, tracking applications, referral and networking messages, thank-you notes; interview prep with a STAR story bank and mock interviews; coding interviews, system design, case rounds and take-homes; salary research, negotiating and comparing offers; career change and positioning; brag documents, self-reviews and promotion cases; hiring: job posts, structured interviews, scorecards. Never invents experience, auto-applies or scrapes job boards. Triggers: "tailor my resume to this job", "review my CV", "write a cover letter", "mock interview me", "prep me for system design", "negotiate this offer", "help me get promoted", "write a job post". LinkedIn profile and posts: linkedin-automation. A designed PDF layout: docs-office.

skills.name: career-ops
skills.purpose: Job-search command center: paste a job description or URL and it scores the role A-F against your CV, writes an evaluation report, generates an ATS-friendly tailored CV (PDF or LaTeX), cover letter and outreach drafts, tracks applications, scans company career portals, and preps interviews (STAR story bank, practice, debrief) and offer negotiation.
skills.how_to_use: Clone the repo (or `npx @santifer/career-ops init`), add cv.md and config/profile.yml, then run `/career-ops {JD or URL}` or a mode such as `scan`, `pdf`, `cover`, `interview-prep`, `offer-prep`, `tracker`. Needs Node and Playwright Chromium for PDFs and portal checks; the router only works inside the repo (it loads modes/*.md and scripts).
skills.evidence: 73.4k stars, created 4 Apr 2026 (formerly santifer/career-ops; went viral after its author used it to land a Head of Applied AI role); #1 repo by stars in GitHub's job-search topic; skills.sh ~750 installs plus many re-hosts; claudemarketplaces 581 installs; in VoltAgent/awesome-agent-skills.
skills.notes: Human-in-the-loop by design: drafts and fills forms but never submits or sends (README, modes/apply.md, modes/email.md). README states no telemetry. Portal scanner uses public Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever APIs plus Playwright/WebSearch; the user carries job-site ToS responsibility. Optional community plugins (Apify, Gmail, Notion) send data to those services; leave them off. package.json postinstall runs `npx playwright install chromium`. Whole-app skill: distil the modes, not the router.

skills.name: job-application-assistant
skills.purpose: One application end to end: fetch and score a posting against your profile, tailor a LaTeX CV, write a cover letter in your own voice (strict anti-cliché style rules), prepare the interview and archive what was submitted.
skills.how_to_use: Clone the repo, run `/setup` to build your profile from a CV or LinkedIn export, then `/apply <url>`; `/rank`, `/outcome` and `/upskill` extend it. Needs a LaTeX toolchain for CV PDFs.
skills.evidence: 44.9k stars, created 18 Mar 2026 by a geophysicist who ran his own search with it; skills.sh ~240 installs; skillsmp lists all its skills.
skills.notes: 09-web-research.md tells the agent to retry 403 pages with curl and a spoofed Chrome User-Agent (after a robots.txt check); drop that when distilling. The repo's separate linkedin-search portal skill scrapes LinkedIn's guest job endpoints and its own SKILL.md says that breaks LinkedIn ToS; the other portal CLIs are Danish job boards. Use only the application-assistant part.

Covers Blender (bpy scripts, headless runs, Blender MCP, modelling, materials, lighting, Cycles/EEVEE renders, export); Three.js scenes (renderer, cameras, PBR materials, HDR lighting, GLTF loaders) and React Three Fiber with drei; slow web 3D (draw calls, instancing, LOD); GLB optimisation (glTF Transform, Draco, Meshopt, KTX2); generative 3D (text or image to 3D with Meshy or Tripo, image to Three.js code); CAD and parametric parts (build123d, OpenSCAD, STEP, STL, 3MF); 3D printing checks, slicing and G-code with OrcaSlicer; OpenUSD, USDZ and Gaussian splats; game-ready assets (budgets, LODs, bakes, colliders, rigs) for Unity, Unreal and Godot. Triggers: "write a Blender script", "model this in 3D", "put a 3D model on my site", "optimize this GLB", "my three.js scene is slow", "turn this image into a 3D model", "design a printable bracket", "slice this STL", "convert this splat to USD". Animating a scene, clip or camera: motion-animation.

skills.how_to_use: `npx skills add earthtojake/text-to-cad --skill cad`. Needs Python 3.11+, `pip install -r requirements.txt` (cadgen[snapshot]) and `playwright install chromium` for snapshots. Triggers on any request to model, edit, export or inspect a 3D part.

skills.notes: Siblings in the same repo: dfam-check (printability per FDM/SLA/SLS/MJF/metal), step-parts (off-the-shelf STEP parts from the third-party catalog api.step.parts, search terms only), dxf, engineering-drawing, bambu-labs, sendcutsend (vendor quoting), urdf/srdf/sdf. The CAD Viewer fetches studio HDRI images from static.morflax.com (CDN images only, no user data sent).
